chunks: Some of our companions, from ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥasanī, from Mālik ibn ʿĀmir, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Zāʾidah, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: Whoever practices religion toward Allah without hearing from a truthful one, Allah will inevitably bind him to hardship; and whoever claims hearing from other than the door which Allah has opened, then he is a mushrik, and that is the trusted door over the hidden secret of Allah.

key_terms.الْبَابِ: the gate or authorized access-point opened by Allah for guidance
key_terms.سَمَاعٍ: receiving religious teaching by hearing from an authorized source
key_terms.سِرِّ اللَّهِ: Allah’s secret, meaning the hidden divine knowledge entrusted to the rightful authority
key_terms.صَادِقٍ: a truthful one, referring here to the divinely reliable guide
key_terms.مُشْرِكٌ: one who commits shirk by associating others in divine authority

ai.seo_question: Why does this hadith say religion must be taken only from the divinely appointed truthful authority?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that true religion must be taken through the divinely appointed truthful authority, not through unauthorized claims or self-derived paths. It warns that departing from the God-opened gate of guidance leads to misguidance and hardship, and it emphasizes the protected status of that divinely entrusted source of sacred knowledge.

en.hubeali: Some of our companions, from Abdul Azeem Bin Abdullah Al Hasany, from Malik Bin Aamir, from Al Mufazzal Bin Zaida, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who makes it a Religion without listening from a Truthful one (Imam<sup>asws</sup>), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Necessitate the hardship to him; and the one who claims to have heard from a door other than which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Opened, so he is a Mushrik (who associates with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>), and that (the Truthful Imam<sup>asws</sup>) is the door of security upon the concealed secrets of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from al-Fudayl from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira who has said the following.

“I said to abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) , ‘the Messenger of Allah has said, “Whoever would die without knowing who his Imam is he would die as if has died in ignorance (of religion).” The Imam (a.s.) said, “That is true.” I then said, “Is it the ignorance of uneducated people or ignorance of ones not knowing his Imam?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “It means the ignorance that is disbelief, hypocrisy and error?”
